title: Malvertising Security POC
subtitle: Authorized testing simulation

data_origin_legend.synthetic: Generated by this POC. Not real telemetry.
data_origin_legend.public: Taken from a public dataset (only if malicious_urls.csv was supplied).
data_origin_legend.calculated: Computed by the metrics engine from the tables above.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.description: Initial control configuration, with the telemetry and rule gaps being tested.

retest.label: Retest (after simulated fixes)
retest.description: Same journeys after: R5 enabled, final-destination evaluation, hop and landing logging repaired, partner domains allow-listed. Two issues are deliberately left open.

assumptions: No Microsoft Sentinel, Bing or Microsoft production telemetry is used.
All journey domains are reserved .test names; IPs are RFC 5737 documentation ranges.
TTD starts at the first redirect hop; TTC starts at alert creation.
Detection latency, triage delay and containment propagation are SIMULATED.
Synthetic credential and download events only; no secret or malware is involved.

rules.name: KNOWN_BAD_DESTINATION
rules.description: Destination domain appears in the threat-intel table

rules.name: FIRST_SEEN_DOMAIN
rules.description: Destination domain is younger than 7 days

rules.name: LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN
rules.description: Hostname contains the protected brand token but is not an approved domain

rules.name: SUSPICIOUS_REDIRECT_CHAIN
rules.description: Two or more redirect hops through a young intermediate host

rules.name: CREDENTIAL_ON_UNAPPROVED_ORIGIN
rules.description: Synthetic credential-entry event on a non-approved authentication origin

rules.name: DOWNLOAD_AFTER_AD_CLICK
rules.description: File download shortly after an ad click

severity_method: POC convention, not an industry standard. High: an expected detection or containment did not occur, or a legitimate destination was blocked. Medium: a visibility or evidence gap while detection still worked. Low: reserved, unused in this POC.
